tools.name: search_tools
tools.description: Search the public MCP server universe by what you want a server to do. Returns compact summaries; call get_server for a full record. Ordered by relevance, except that results with official_match true come first and results with has_public_source true come next. official_match is true when the server

tools.name: get_server
tools.description: Return the full registry record for one MCP server, its verification facts, and which clients it can be installed into. This data comes from the Official MCP Registry.

tools.name: get_install_config
tools.description: Return a ready-to-run install command, or the exact configuration fragment, for one MCP server and one client. This data comes from the Official MCP Registry.

findings.title: Anomalously long tool description
findings.detail: Description of "search_tools" is 2854 chars, far longer than this server's median (167). Overlong descriptions are a common place to bury instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search_tools · Private data: search_tools, get_server · Public sink: search_tools · Destructive: search_tools, get_install_config.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search_tools · Private data: search_tools, get_server · Public sink: search_tools · Destructive: search_tools, get_install_config

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "search_tools" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
